hyps.why: Node 2 only reaches the output through edge 5, so with edge 5 removed an upgrade on edge 1 cannot affect the output.
Edge 2 feeds node 2, which is dead-ended when edge 5 is none, so the edit has no useful effect.
With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 4 processes nothing.
With node 1 disconnected from the input, edge 2 carries no signal, so upgrading it does not help.
Replacing none with a conv on the direct input-output edge adds a whole path and gains more than replacing another op.
Adding a skip as a new direct path gives a large gain compared with replacing an existing op, since it aids gradient flow.
Replacing none on the final edge opens the path through node 2 and gains more than swapping among non-none ops.
Replacing none with a conv on edge 4 restores a major path to the output, so the gain is large.
With one alternative route to the output removed, a strong op on the direct edge matters more.
Without the direct edge 0->3, the output depends more on edge 5, so a stronger op there has a bigger effect.
